The other metrics

Academia invented quite a few. Here they all are, with the fine print.

g-index
7
Largest g whose top g papers share at least g² citations. Egghe (2006), for people who felt the h-index undervalued their best paper.
e-index
6
The surplus citations in the h-core that the h-index quietly ignores. Zhang (2009).
m-quotient
1.33
h-index per year since the first paper. Hirsch (2005) called 1 “successful” and 2 “outstanding”, after twenty years. It has been 3.
hI-index
0.57
The h-index shared out among all 28 authors of the h-core papers. Batista et al. (2006). Collaboration, penalised.
i100-index
0
Papers with at least 100 citations. Google's i10-index, made aspirational.
Uncited papers
3
Papers nobody has cited yet. Give them a minute.
Authors per paper
8.62
Average author-list length. Science is a team sport; bibliometrics is not.
First-author papers
4 of 9
Where my name comes first. Some committees count only these, so here they are.

None of these say whether the work is any good. For how research ought to be assessed, see DORA and the Leiden Manifesto.
